paragraphs: By way of introduction, my name is Joshua Chappell. My intent is to apply for the Social Media Manager position at Muck Rack. I feel I have a lot of immediate value I can bring to your organization.

Your posting asks for someone creative, organized and metrics-driven, with experience in video production, scripting and editing. Video is the core of my work. At Charter One I created and led a social media content initiative that drove more than 20x the engagement of standard content, and I led video initiatives that drove paid and organic engagement by over 100%. At Grand Canyon Education I scripted original organic content with the marketing team and delivered 200+ videos over two years reaching millions on TV, paid social, and organic channels. I script, shoot, and edit in-house, so your social calendar does not wait on an outside crew.

On the paid side, I generated leads with Facebook ads for my own company and integrated on-site call-to-action elements with the Facebook pixel to monitor ad performance. At Charter One I created and led a video initiative that raised click-through rates for running ads by over 200%. I hold a Master's in Marketing with a Marketing Analytics specialization. You also ask for AI tools in day-to-day work: I used Claude agentic coding to build content workflows that cut production times in half. Your customers are PR and communications professionals. At the Arizona State Legislature I synchronized with Communications teams across legislative bodies and chambers, so I have worked alongside the people your platform serves.
Thank you for taking the time out of your busy day to read my letter. I look forward to the opportunity of doing an interview with you.

> NOT THE FULL POSTING. No job-board tool (Dice, ZipRecruiter, Indeed) returned this job's description, and the employer's Greenhouse page (https://job-boards.greenhouse.io/muckrack/jobs/8858924002) could not be fetched. The lines below are the only exact phrases from the posting that came back in WebSearch snippets (from the Greenhouse, Built In, Working Nomads, Remote Front, Glassdoor and NetInfluencer copies). They are fragments, not in the posting's original order, and most of the posting is missing. Open the Greenhouse link for the full text.

## Role description (fragments)

- "creative, organized and metrics-driven"
- "supports paid social advertising, employee advocacy, competitive tracking, crisis management, and video production across LinkedIn, Instagram, TikTok, and X"
- "How success will be measured in this role"

## Qualifications (fragments)

- "5+ years professional experience, with as many years of related experience (directly in social media management)"
- "Experience developing and executing social media strategies for B2B companies (preferably SaaS) for LinkedIn, Instagram, TikTok and X"
- "Experience with video production, scripting and editing"
- "Experience with social listening and competitive tracking"
- "experience with social listening and competitive tracking, employee advocacy and experience with reputation management"
- "experience with running and optimizing paid social media advertising"
- "Proficient in Sprout Social"
- "Comfortable with tools including Muck Rack, Google Analytics"
- "Data-driven mindset"
- "Proactively incorporate AI tools into day to day work to improve productively and accelerate delivery"

## Travel and location (fragments)

- "up to 10% travel and expected attendance at an annual company offsite"

## Compensation (fragments)

## About Muck Rack (fragment)

- "the leading SaaS platform for public relations and communications professionals"

research.overview: Muck Rack makes PR and communications software: a media/journalist database, media monitoring, and coverage reporting. It is self-funded and has been remote-first for over a decade. Its job postings say it has pledged to stay fully distributed. Headcount estimates range from about 290 (TrueUp) to 478 (Revelio Labs, 2025). Sacra estimates ARR at $108M in April 2026, up about 25% year over year; this is a third-party estimate. Muck Rack bought Keyhole, a social listening and analytics tool, in August 2024 and Ruepoint, a media intelligence firm, in January 2025. Gregory Galant is still listed as co-founder and CEO, and no 2026 CEO change turned up. The Social Media Manager role (Built In job 11448070) is fully remote in the US and pays $97K-$120K plus a quarterly bonus. It covers B2B SaaS social strategy, paid social, employee advocacy, social listening, and crisis/reputation work across LinkedIn, Instagram, TikTok, and X, with up to 10% travel and an annual offsite. An earlier Built In posting for the same title (job 3313829) was for the company's first-ever Social Media Manager and was taken down on Nov 18, 2024, so the current opening may be a backfill. Most employee reviews are company-wide or from sales roles. Only 3 Glassdoor reviews are tagged Marketing, and several of those date from 2020-2022. The Indeed MCP connector failed to connect for this session, so Indeed data comes only from web search.

glassdoor.rating: About 3.9 to 4.1 out of 5. The figure varies by regional Glassdoor snapshot; the US page showed 4.0-4.1.
glassdoor.review_count: About 132 to 137 company-wide reviews, depending on snapshot. Only 3 are tagged Marketing (4.9 average), and several of those are from 2020-2022.
glassdoor.summary: Company-wide, 65-68% of reviewers would recommend Muck Rack to a friend. Work-life balance scores about 4.3, culture and values about 3.8, compensation and benefits about 3.7, and career opportunities lowest at about 3.5-3.6. Positive reviews praise the coworkers, the remote setup, benefits and PTO, and the product's reputation. Negative reviews cluster in sales and go-to-market roles. They describe a turnover spike in 2025 that included managers and VPs, favoritism, promotions tied to loyalty to leadership, an unsettled sales team structure, slower SDR promotion, and one claim that headcount is being cut through performance pressure and quiet exits instead of announced layoffs. A July 2026 Account Executive review is titled 'Known product overshadowed by poor leadership and favoritism.' The 3 Marketing reviews are positive. One mentions Slack feeling 'always on' and pay needing an update; another says growth paths within roles are not always clear. Three reviews is too few to represent the marketing team.

indeed.rating: 1.0 out of 5, from what appears to be a single review
indeed.summary: Web search surfaced one Indeed review, dated July 30, 2025, from a sales employee in New York State. It says the sales culture 'has become toxic,' that about 10% of AEs made quota over the last 2 years, and that sales leadership lacks transparency and shows favoritism. One review is too small a sample to draw a company-wide conclusion, and it is sales-specific. The Indeed MCP connector failed to connect (rate-limit/protocol error), so get_company_data could not be run to confirm the rating or review count.

reddit.summary: Several searches (site:reddit.com, 'reddit working there', 'reddit interview/job offer') returned no Reddit threads about working at Muck Rack. Every result came from Glassdoor, job boards, or product review sites.

pros.point: Remote-first for over a decade, with a stated pledge never to force staff back into an office. The company was named to Built In's 2024 Best Places to Work in remote categories. Glassdoor rates work-life balance about 4.3 of 5.
Reviewers across Glassdoor praise coworkers as friendly and collaborative. Some call it the best company they have worked for in years.

Benefits include unplugged vacation time and a 401(k) with employer contributions. A 'select' health plan covers 100% of the premium for individuals and 85% for dependents. Remote staff get a home office stipend, coworking memberships, and internet and phone reimbursement.
US pay is geo-neutral: it is set by job level and function, not location, and reviewed at least once a year. The Social Media Manager role lists $97K-$120K plus a quarterly bonus.

The product has a strong reputation, which helps a social role selling to PR and comms buyers. Employees call it one of the few reputable PR platforms, and G2 shows 4.6 from 392 product reviews. The Keyhole acquisition adds social listening tools that match the role's social listening and reputation duties.
No known layoffs per TrueUp. Revelio Labs shows 2.3% headcount growth from 2024 to 2025. Muck Rack calls itself self-funded, and Sacra estimates ARR growth of about 25% to $108M in April 2026.

The few marketing-tagged Glassdoor reviews are positive (3 reviews, 4.9 average). They cite remote work, benefits, internal transparency, and the chance to move between departments. The sample is small and partly old.

cons.point: Reviewers report a turnover spike in 2025, including 'many well-respected managers and VPs' across the go-to-market org. Marketing often sits in that org at SaaS companies.

Favoritism and politics come up repeatedly: promotions are tied to loyalty to leadership, people are let go for dissenting views, and leadership ignores feedback from high performers. One July 2026 review says this outright.

One 2-star sales review says leadership is cutting headcount through performance pressure and quiet exits instead of transparent layoffs. Revelio Labs also shows active job postings down 58% in 2025. This could mean slower hiring, but it is not a confirmed cut.
Career growth is the lowest-rated Glassdoor category (about 3.5-3.6). Reviewers describe unclear advancement paths, including a marketing reviewer, and slowed upward mobility for SDRs.

Pay and benefits complaints: compensation and benefits rate about 3.7. Raises for internal promotions reportedly lag the external market, one marketing reviewer said pay needed updating, and health insurance is described as 'not particularly amazing.'

Workload and availability: a marketing reviewer says Slack can feel 'always on,' and another reviewer says staff can be expected to do the jobs of 2-3 people. Both matter for a solo social role that also covers crisis management.

The sales org appears strained. RepVue reports about 25-34% of reps hitting quota against a 44% industry average, and a culture and leadership score of 3.3. The Indeed reviewer claims about 10% of AEs made quota. Pressure on revenue can reach marketing and demand-gen teams.

red_flags: Several Glassdoor reviews from 2025-2026 describe go-to-market turnover, favoritism, and poor mid-level leadership. The newest critical review found is from July 2026, so this is a current issue. Ask which org the social role reports into and how long its leader has been there.

One review alleges headcount is being cut through performance pressure and quiet exits instead of announced layoffs. TrueUp lists no known layoffs, so ask directly about attrition and any reductions in 2025-2026.

Muck Rack posted its first-ever Social Media Manager role in 2024 (taken down Nov 18, 2024) and is hiring for the title again in 2026. Ask whether this is a backfill, what happened to the previous hire, and whether the role is a team of one.
The role lists crisis management and reputation monitoring, and a marketing reviewer says Slack feels 'always on.' Ask about after-hours and weekend coverage expectations.
Low sales quota attainment (RepVue 25-34% vs 44% industry average) can mean pressure on marketing to produce pipeline. Ask how social success is measured (brand vs pipeline metrics).
The marketing-specific evidence is thin: only 3 Glassdoor reviews, several from 2020-2022. Most negative detail comes from sales roles. Ask to speak with a current marketing team member.
Indeed's 1.0 rating rests on one review, and the Indeed connector was unavailable, so the Indeed rating could not be verified.
research.bottom_line: For a remote US social media role, Muck Rack has real strengths: a long record as a remote-first company with a pledge to stay that way, geo-neutral pay of $97K-$120K plus a quarterly bonus, solid benefits, a well-known product, and apparent revenue growth with no reported layoffs. Overall reviews sit around 4.0 on Glassdoor. The main risk is a cluster of 2025-2026 reviews describing go-to-market turnover, favoritism, and weak leadership, though most of those come from sales. Marketing-specific reviews are few and partly old, so they do not settle how the marketing team runs today. Before accepting, Joshua should ask who the role reports to and how long that person has been there, whether this is a backfill of the 2024 first-ever social hire, how big the team is, what after-hours crisis coverage is expected, and how success will be measured.
